title: Connection strings with an empty or omitted password
summary: Connection strings with the password slot present but empty (user followed by a colon and then the at-sign, password:'', Password=;) or omitted entirely (user only, keyword absent), across MySQL, PostgreSQL, Redis and OLE DB forms.
rationale: There is no secret to cover. A reported range would be a false alarm over the user name or host, and a masked empty value would corrupt a configuration that is deliberately passwordless (socket or interactive-prompt authentication). The grammars state the empty and omitted forms explicitly, so this does not depend on judging how a value looks.

expectation.rationale: The vendor pages show the empty-password forms (a colon after the user name with no password; password:''; Password=; in an OLE DB string) and the omitted forms (user only; redis user and password optional). A string whose password position holds no characters contains no password.

sources.supports: To connect without a password place a colon after the user name and do not specify a password (mysqlx://user_name:@localhost); the key-value form is {user:'user_name', password:'', host:'localhost'}.
sources.locator: password discussion in the connection-string section

sources.supports: The URI userspec is user[:password], so the password may be absent; in keyword/value form an empty value is written with single quotes.
sources.locator: sections 32.1.1.2 Connection URIs and 32.1.1.1 Keyword/Value Connection Strings

sources.supports: In redis://user:password@host:port/dbnum the user, password and dbnum are optional.
An OLE DB example shows User ID=Admin;Password=; and says the User ID and Password keywords are optional if the database is unsecured.
